writeup: TIC 308574817 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 4.6 days, detected in automated TESS photometry data. The system shows a primary eclipse with a dimming depth of 11.30 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal achieved a high detection significance of 132.8 in the BLS analysis, and pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 23.8, though the centroid offset of 0.7 arcseconds warrants note. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipse depths differ significantly, suggesting the true orbital period may be double the initial measurement. Despite this period ambiguity, pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain consistent with the corrected 4.6-day period reported here.
